newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures fall in line with gas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures fall in line with gas.

text.p: The NYMEX electricity futures complex fell sharply for the second consecutive day amid cooler temperatures in the western U.S. and lower natural gas prices, market sources said Thursday.
In addition, traders said the impending restart of power generation units including the 1,080 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear plant in California added to the market's weak tone.
The nuclear unit is scheduled to restart Friday after shutting for unplanned maintenance on September 24.
The November California-Oregon border (COB) NYMEX contract lost 30 cents to settle at $17.30 per megawatt hour (MWh), while December fell 11 cents to $18.69.
Palo Verde for November fell 15 cents to $17.00 per MWh, while December fell 22 cents to $17.38.
"There is good support slightly below where the market was trading at today--it bounced back up from those levels several times," said one market source.
NYMEX said that a total of 206 Palo Verde and 641 COB contracts had traded.
